messages.content: "Imagine you are a drone operator. You are currently operating a drone that is at a point (5, 7) in the sky. You are asked to move the drone to a new point (10, 15). After reaching the new point, you are again asked to move the drone to another point (20, 25). Can you calculate the total distance the drone has traveled using the Euclidean norm method?"

function.name: math_hypot
function.description: Calculate the Euclidean norm, sqrt(sum(squares)), the length of the vector from the origin to point (x, y) which is the hypotenuse of the right triangle. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

z.description: Optional. The z-coordinate value. Default is 0.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to calculate total distance traveled by moving from (5,7) to (10,15), then to (20,25). They want Euclidean norm method. We need to compute distances between successive points and sum them.

We can use the provided function math_hypot. But we need to call it twice: once for distance between (5,7) and (10,15), and once for distance between (10,15) and (20,25). Then sum.

We should call the function with arguments: x difference and y difference? Actually math_hypot expects coordinates relative to origin. So we can compute differences: dx1=10-5=5, dy1=15-7=8. Then call math_hypot(x=5,y=8). That returns sqrt(5^2+8^2)=sqrt(25+64)=sqrt(89)=9.433... Similarly second segment: dx2=20-10=10, dy2=25-15=10. Call math_hypot(x=10,y=10). That returns sqrt(100+100)=sqrt(200)=14.142... Sum: 9.433... + 14.142... = 23.575... approx.
